standard_prerequisites.name: Domination of complete surjections
standard_prerequisites.use: Produce the common dominating factorization S'' -> S x_B S' used to reduce to comparable factorizations.

standard_prerequisites.name: Regular sequence lifting
standard_prerequisites.use: Drive the comparable-factorization step: lifting regular sequences through flat maps and joining them.

core_obligations: Reduce to complete S: complete the factorization, verify it stays good, transfer the regular-sequence condition through completion (displayed identities).
Reduce two arbitrary factorizations to comparable ones via the fibre product S x_B S' and the dominating factorization.
For comparable A -> S' -> S -> B: the kernel of S' -> S is generated by a regular sequence obtained from the surjection of regular local fibres, lifted via Grothendieck's lemma.

Join both directions: if Ker(S -> B) is regular then so is Ker(S' -> B) (join lemma); conversely split the minimal generating system of J = Ker(S' -> B) along the lifted regular sequence and read off Ker(S -> B).
proof_roadmap: Normalize to complete factorizations, reduce to comparable ones, and prove the comparability step in both directions with the displayed lifting and joining arguments.
difficulty_reason: The independence theorem underpinning every CI-homomorphism statement; the comparable-factorization analysis is a genuine multi-step argument.
